transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-05-09 08:30 PT | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Nina (Redwood Solutions), Tomas (Redwood CSM), Priya (Head of ML), Mark (CTO), Jae (Backend), Lena (Product), Evan (Security)

---
Summary: Brief kickoff to align success criteria, workload sizing, timeline, and the cost model for the pilot. Customer emphasized cost predictability and ability to degrade gracefully during peak traffic.
Topics: Success criteria, traffic profile, per-token economics, batching/caching knobs, benchmark plan and timeline, security gating.

Action items (captured at top, see metadata): see action_items field.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining. quick intros so we know who's on the line — from our side it's alex, samir the se, nina on solutions and tomas for success. and you all?
[00:12] Priya: hi i'm priya, head of ml. we own the models and the inference budget.
[00:16] Mark: mark here, cto. i'll be involved on infra/ops decisions.
[00:20] Jae: jae, backend eng. i'll run the traffic replay and assist with endpoints.
[00:25] Lena: lena, product, i'm here for success metrics.
[00:28] Evan: evan, security/compliance, i'll validate policies and SOC2/SSO details.
[00:33] Alex: great, order of ops — align on what success looks like, capture traffic profile and token stats, agree on bench plan and timeline, and then run a 48-72h benchmark with replayed traffic.
[00:45] Samir: quick note — our pilot typically runs in three phases: sizing & replay, controlled benchmark with variances (batching, quantized vs fp16), and then a week of smoke in their environment for end-to-end validation.
[00:56] Priya: that sounds right. for context our main call is augment-recommendation for checkout, about 1M calls/day during promos, baseline 95th pct latency goal is ~350ms server-side. our current provider has 95p around 450ms under load.
[01:15] Alex: ok good. can you share the token distribution? average prompt and completion lengths?
[01:22] Priya: yeah average input is ~120 tokens, average output 280, tails go up to 2k but that's <0.5% of requests.
[01:33] Samir: cool. rough arithmetic: at 1M calls/day with 400 avg tokens total, that's 400M tokens/day, which is big. we need to look at batching and prefix caching.
[01:46] Mark: wait 400M tokens/day — does that assume every call is full generation? some of our flows are rerank-only which are shorter.
[01:53] Priya: right, we have three flows: short rerank (~40 tokens), medium augmentation (~400 tokens), long analysis (~1500 tokens) but long is rare. distribution is 65% medium, 25% short, 10% long.
[02:08] Nina: good to have that split — it changes batching strategy. for short flows we can use batching aggressively; for medium we target streaming-friendly batch sizes.
[02:18] Jae: our SLAs for checkout are strict — we can't have tail latency spikes that block cart flows. so if batching increases 95p beyond 350ms that's bad.
[02:29] Samir: understood. two knobs we tune: batch size and batch timeout. plus KV cache for prefix state — if recommendation prompts share prefixes, cache hits reduce compute and reduce tokens served to the model.
[02:42] Priya: do you have any examples of per-token cost after batching and caching?
[02:46] Alex: yes, we'll send a detailed sheet but rough numbers today: raw hosted per-token unit at baseline model A is $0.00012/token before batching; with batching improvements and prefix KV cache we often see effective token spend drop 30-55% depending on hit rates. so effective can be ~ $0.00005 - $0.00009/token.
[03:10] Mark: that's a wide range. what assumptions drive the 55%?
[03:13] Samir: mainly heavy cache hits plus continuous batching across many concurrent requests and using a quantized model variant for medium-length sequences. Also sequence length distributions and hardware kernel efficiencies.
[03:25] Priya: what's the tradeoff if we pin dedicated instances vs hosted?
[03:29] Nina: Dedicated gives more predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale because you amortize GPU occupancy; hosted is faster to start and we can scale dynamically but cost per token can be higher under sustained heavy load. For pilot we usually run hosted but with a dedicated-capacity option in the benchmark to show delta.
[03:47] Lena: can we set a runbook for graceful degradation? e.g., switch to shorter responses or rerank-only during peak?
[03:53] Samir: yes, we support policy-based routing: if latency > threshold switch to cheaper model or shorter output tokens. We can simulate that in the benchmark.
[04:02] Evan: from a security perspective we need to know data residency, KMS usage, and audit logs. SOC2 docs would be required before Prod.
[04:09] Alex: we'll share SOC2 doc and the KMS integrations page. Nina will drop a secure-arch brief.
[04:15] Priya: timeline — we're aiming to have pilot results to show execs in 6 weeks. is that feasible?
[04:20] Alex: yes, typical 4-8 week pilots fit. Proposed schedule: week 0 (this week) collect traces + requirements, week 1 prepare replay + bench infra, week 2 run initial bench with model variant 1, week 3 tune batching/cache, week 4 run long 48-72h run, week 5 analyze and compile econ model, week 6 present findings.
[04:41] Mark: we also need to measure 95th pct cost-per-request and SLO violations per 100k requests.
[04:48] Samir: agreed — we'll capture p50/p90/p95 latency, tokens per request, compute ms per token, GPU occupancy, effective cost per request, and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:59] Priya: what are the model variants you plan to bench?
[05:03] Samir: we'll run 3: model A (fp16 baseline), model B (quantized int8 with slightly lower quality), model C (smaller architecture for short flows only). We'll also test batching configs (max batch sizes 8/16/32 and timeouts 5/10/20ms) and cache hit rates simulated at 10/30/60%.
[05:22] Jae: for replay we use our staging logs — is there a recommended anonymization?
[05:27] Nina: remove PII, replace user ids with consistent pseudonyms to preserve repetitive patterns, and obfuscate product ids if needed but keep distribution. an export csv with timestamp, flow type, prompt token count, and response token count is ideal.
[05:39] Priya: we'll produce that. any particular infra hooks? ports or agent?
[05:44] Alex: we can do either hosted replay by uploading logs to a secure bucket we provide, or do the replay from your infra via a temporary token. we'll prefer secure bucket for reproducibility.
[05:55] Evan: we need encryption at rest and key control if logs are in your bucket. KMS integration duration?
[06:00] Nina: our storage uses customer-managed keys for Private deployments; for hosted pilot we can enable server-side encryption with customer KMS where required. we'll note details in the secure brief.
[06:11] Lena: back to cost — can you produce a per-1k-token estimate for our mix?
[06:15] Alex: yes — rough calc on the call: using sample distribution (65% medium, 25% short, 10% long) and base per-token $0.00012 for model A, base daily token 400M yields raw cost $48k/day. After batching and cache (assume 30% effective reduction) that becomes ~$33.6k/day, or about $0.000084/token. Per-1k-token that is $0.084.
[06:43] Priya: our budget target is < $0.06 per 1k tokens effective for the pilot to be interesting.
[06:50] Samir: to get to $0.06 we'd need either higher cache hit rates (~50%) or quantized/dedicated savings, or reduce avg tokens via shorter responses. We'll model those scenarios in the worksheet.
[07:03] Mark: can you show the math for dedicated GPU amortization?
[07:07] Samir: high level: dedicated reduces per-token infer costs by improving GPU utilization and removing multi-tenant overhead. we'll simulate a monthly committed capacity with expected peak throughput and compute occupancy curves; it's in the pricelist appendix.
[07:18] Priya: do we need to pin model versions during bench or can you fallback to equivalent variants?
[07:22] Alex: for consistent benchmarks we pin exact model weights and environment. fallback policies are for prod resilience but we won't enable fallback during controlled bench unless we test that scenario explicitly.
[07:33] Jae: instrumentation — what tracers should we add to our app to capture latencies?
[07:37] Samir: capture request enqueue time, send time, service response time, token counts, and model variant tag. also capture cache hit/miss events. we provide a small SDK snippet to emit those metrics.
[07:49] Evan: will there be any data exfil concerns while you run the benchmark?
[07:52] Nina: no, replay is deterministic; we only ingest anonymized prompts and token counts. we can sign an NDA addendum if needed.
[07:59] Priya: ok, next steps recap?
[08:02] Alex: alex to send pilot pricing worksheet and example econ scenarios; samir to send bench plan; priya to share anonymized logs; nina to send SOC2 + arch brief; evan to confirm security questions. schedule bench window for week of 2028-05-22.
[08:18] Mark: sounds good. also include a small appendix with cost sensitivity to average output length — that's our main lever.
[08:25] Samir: yes we'll include sensitivity charts: cost vs cache hit rate, cost vs avg tokens, cost vs batch timeout.
[08:33] Lena: please call out any quality tradeoffs when using quantized models. product needs an estimated QA delta.
[08:39] Samir: we'll put quality regression estimates and suggested eval prompts for you to run.
[08:45] Alex: cool. any other Qs?
[08:47] Evan: one sec on SSO, i'll send a list of identity providers and the SAML metadata.
[08:50] Priya: no more from me. excited to see the numbers.
[08:53] Alex: great — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts and lock the replay window.
[08:57] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard names and minor punctuation issues. Speaker overlaps around 00:45-01:15 where multiple folks chimed in about token math.
